name: Oral Submucous Fibrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Oral Submucous Fibrosis

criteria.description: Fibrosis and blanching of the buccal mucosa and other oral mucosal sites
Histopathological evidence of subepithelial fibrosis with hyalinization
Burning sensation in the oral mucosa on spicy food intake
Pale, stiff oral mucosa with loss of elasticity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive mouth opening limitation with clinical evidence of mucosal fibrosis confirmed by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathological confirmation; exclusion of other causes of oral fibrosis is essential.

laboratory: Elevated serum levels of collagen markers
Increased inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing submucosal fibrosis and muscle involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible genetic susceptibility in some populations
other: Histopathology showing epithelial atrophy, juxta-epithelial fibrosis, and hyalinization
Immunohistochemistry may show altered collagen type expression

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement including skin thickening beyond oral cavity
Absence of progressive fibrosis and trismus
Presence of ulcerative or exophytic lesions

redFlags: Signs suggestive of malignant transformation (induration, ulceration, lymphadenopathy)
references: Gupta D, et al. Oral submucous fibrosis: A review. J Oral Pathol Med. 2020;49(8):689-696.
Rajendran R. Oral submucous fibrosis: etiology, pathogenesis, and future research. Bull World Health Organ. 1994;72(6):985-996.
Warnakulasuriya S. Oral submucous fibrosis: a review of aetiology and pathogenesis. Oral Oncol. 1992;28(3):167-172.
